entries.summary: bot-turn-outcome.v1 runs every rule that reads only the outcome (#1375), so the device refuses a violating outcome on submit_result and the model corrects it in the same Turn. New contract-mismatch keywords: duplicate-target (a repeated delegate to, this Bot included), duplicate-local-id (create_bot), duplicate-id (cancel_routine, cancel_delegation), duplicate-member (room_call, create_room, update_room), admin-not-member (create_room), empty-update (update_routine with neither schedule nor prompt, update_bot or update_room with no field), and schedule-invalid, schedule-unreachable, schedule-beyond-horizon, tz-invalid for a schedule that checkRoutineSchedule refuses. The routine calendar moved from @byok-sdk/core to @byok-sdk/protocol: import checkRoutineSchedule, nextRoutineOccurrence, the ROUTINE_* constants and their types from @byok-sdk/protocol. Core drops them and its routine_schedule_invalid code; nextRoutineOccurrence throws the protocol RoutineScheduleError (code routine_schedule_invalid) instead of ByokCoreError. A repeated daysOfWeek day is schedule_invalid instead of being merged. A routine already stored with a repeated weekday (for example by the byok-mcp-server example) throws RoutineScheduleError when its next occurrence is computed: update it to distinct days before the upgrade. The schedule fragment has one closed shape without the oneOf: RoutineScheduleShape and the scheduleShape option are removed, and a schema over budget is schema-over-budget with no flat fallback. The room mode enum and RoomFields.mode have only 'mention'. K8 drops its apply-time copies of these rules and the delegation reason duplicate_target; the owner updateRoutine and the sealed create and reseal check an empty update and the calendar at their entry. A Host that vendors K8 copies the changed files and imports the calendar from @byok-sdk/protocol. K8 also publishes two new projection prefixes (#1393): room-seat:<roomId>:<seatId> when a room seat becomes terminal (post, pass, failed, busy, removed or blocked), and room-root:<roomId>:<root> when every seat of a round root is terminal; advanceRoomSeats takes a publish argument. The Host must handle both prefixes before it upgrades, since a Host that refuses an unknown projection prefix fails its flush on the first one. Room message retention (#1394, migration: examples/bot-collaboration/README.md#retention): K8 retainRoots now also moves room messages out of the collaboration state (#1394), with or without roomHistory: each message whose round root or seat is no longer in the state, except the last contextTurnLimit messages of its room, becomes an archived row in namespace roomMessages, keyed by message id. The same call lowers each visibleFrom offset by the messages it moves from before it, so every member's seat ContextPack keeps the same messages; historyWindow.omittedMessages and notice count only messages still in the state, as omittedTurns does. The Room shape and the state version do not change. snapshot().team.rooms no longer holds the whole room history: a Host that turns roomHistory on should do so before the first retention; after a retention, its backfill also reads the roomMessages archived rows, which the owner switch export carries in its archived section. A Host that vendored K8 copies the new src/retention.ts, src/rules/rooms.ts and src/retention-vectors.test-support.ts, and adds archived(namespace, id) to its RetentionSubject.
